npm-vite.title: “node” or “npm” is not recognized
npm-vite.symptom: The terminal says 'node' is not recognized as an internal or external command (Windows), or command not found: npm (macOS and Linux).
causes: Node.js is not installed.
Node.js was installed after the terminal was opened, so the terminal doesn't know where to find it yet.

diagnose.text: Ask for the installed versions. Each command should print a version number.

fix.text: Install Node.js 22.12 or newer from https://nodejs.org/ (24 LTS is recommended; npm is included), then close the terminal and open a new one.

npm-vite.confirm: node --version prints v22.12 or newer, and npm --version prints a version.

npm-vite.title: npm warns about an unsupported engine, or Vite asks for a newer Node.js
npm-vite.symptom: npm install prints “npm warn EBADENGINE Unsupported engine”, or npm run dev prints “Vite requires Node.js version 20.19+ or 22.12+”.
causes: Your Node.js is older than 22.12, the version the project's package.json asks for.

diagnose.text: Check the version.

fix.text: Install the current LTS version from https://nodejs.org/, open a new terminal, then install the dependencies again.

npm-vite.confirm: node --version prints v22.12 or newer and npm install finishes without the engine warning.

npm-vite.title: npm can't find package.json
npm-vite.symptom: npm prints “npm error code ENOENT” and “Could not read package.json”.
causes: The terminal is open in a different folder from the project.
The ZIP was extracted into a folder of the same name, so the project is one level deeper.

diagnose.text: List the files in the current folder. You should see package.json and src.

fix.text: Move into the folder that contains package.json with cd, for example cd my-project, and run the command again.

npm-vite.title: npm install fails with ETIMEDOUT, ECONNRESET or ENOTFOUND
npm-vite.symptom: npm install stops with a network error code such as ETIMEDOUT, ECONNRESET or ENOTFOUND.
causes: There is no internet connection, or it dropped during the download.
The network (for example a college network) only allows access through a proxy.

diagnose.text: Check that npm can reach its registry. A working connection prints PONG.

fix.text: Reconnect and run npm install again; packages it already downloaded are reused from npm's cache. On a network that needs a proxy, ask the network administrator how to configure it.

npm-vite.confirm: npm install finishes and prints how many packages were added.

npm-vite.title: “npm.ps1 cannot be loaded because running scripts is disabled”
npm-vite.symptom: In Windows PowerShell, every npm command fails with a message about npm.ps1 and running scripts being disabled.
causes: PowerShell's execution policy blocks .ps1 scripts, and PowerShell tried npm.ps1.

diagnose.text: The message names npm.ps1, which confirms it is the execution policy and not a missing installation.

fix.text: Call npm.cmd instead, which the execution policy doesn't block, or open Command Prompt instead of PowerShell and use npm as usual.
The project's README also mentions Set-ExecutionPolicy. That changes a PowerShell setting for your user account; the steps above work without changing any setting.

npm-vite.title: The app opens on port 5174 (or another number) instead of 5173
npm-vite.symptom: npm run dev prints “Port 5173 is in use, trying another one...” and then a different address.
causes: Another Vite dev server, often an earlier copy of this project, is still running and using port 5173.

diagnose.text: Look for other terminal windows or tabs that are still running npm run dev.

fix.text: Use the address Vite prints; the app works the same on any port. Or stop the other server with Ctrl+C in its terminal and start this one again.
Saved data belongs to one address. If the app looks empty on the new port, your data is still saved under the old address.

npm-vite.confirm: The app opens at the address Vite printed.

npm-vite.title: The browser shows a blank page or an error overlay
npm-vite.symptom: npm run dev is running, but the page is empty or covered by an error message.
causes: A change in the code has a syntax error or throws an error while the page loads.

diagnose.text: Read the terminal running npm run dev and the browser's console (press F12, then open Console). The first red error names a file and a line.

fix.text: Open that file at that line and fix the error, or undo your last change. Vite reloads the page when you save.

npm-vite.confirm: The page loads and the console shows no red errors.

npm-vite.title: npm run dev works, but npm run build fails with TypeScript errors
npm-vite.symptom: npm run build stops with errors such as “error TS2322: Type … is not assignable to type …”.
causes: The build script runs tsc --noEmit before vite build. The dev server doesn't type-check, so type errors only appear when you build.

diagnose.text: List every type error with its file and line, without building.

fix.text: Fix each error at the line it names, starting with the first one; later errors are often caused by earlier ones.

npm-vite.confirm: npm run build finishes and lists the files it wrote to dist.

npm-vite.title: npm ci says package.json and package-lock.json are not in sync
npm-vite.symptom: npm ci stops with “npm ci can only install packages when your package.json and package-lock.json … are in sync”.
causes: package.json was edited (for example a dependency was added by hand) without updating package-lock.json.

diagnose.text: Compare the dependencies in package.json with what you changed recently.

fix.text: Run npm install, which updates package-lock.json to match package.json. Keep both files together in version control.

npm-vite.confirm: npm ci finishes without the error.

npm-vite.title: Strange errors after switching Node.js versions or adding packages
npm-vite.symptom: Commands that used to work now fail with errors inside node_modules, for example about a missing module or a native binary.
causes: node_modules was installed with a different Node.js version or is out of date with package-lock.json.

diagnose.text: Check which Node.js version you are using now.

fix.text: Reinstall exactly what package-lock.json lists. npm ci removes the old node_modules folder itself before installing.

npm-vite.confirm: npm run dev and npm test work again.

npm-vite.title: npm test shows FAIL after I changed something
npm-vite.symptom: npm test prints FAIL next to a test file and an AssertionError with “expected” and “received” values.
causes: You changed text, behaviour or a calculation that a test checks.

diagnose.text: Read the failing test's name and compare the expected and received values. Open the test file at the line shown.

fix.text: If the change was a mistake, fix the code. If the new behaviour is what you want, update the test's expected value and explain the change in your report.

npm-vite.confirm: npm test reports that every test passed.

python-streamlit.title: “python” is not recognized, or it opens the Microsoft Store
python-streamlit.symptom: The terminal says 'python' is not recognized (Windows) or command not found: python3 (macOS and Linux), or typing python opens the Microsoft Store.
causes: Python is not installed, or it was installed without being added to PATH.
On Windows, the Microsoft Store shortcut named python.exe runs instead of a real installation.

diagnose.text: Ask for the version. It must print Python 3.11 or newer.

fix.text: Install Python 3.11 or newer from https://www.python.org/downloads/. On Windows, tick “Add python.exe to PATH” in the installer. Then open a new terminal.
On Windows you can also use the Python launcher, which the python.org installer adds.

python-streamlit.confirm: python --version (Windows) or python3 --version (macOS, Linux) prints Python 3.11 or newer.

python-streamlit.title: My Python is older than 3.11
python-streamlit.symptom: python3 --version prints a version below 3.11 (for example Python 3.9), or pip reports that a package requires a different Python.
causes: The python3 command runs an older Python, for example one that came with the operating system or developer tools.

diagnose.text: Check which Python the command runs and its version.

fix.text: Install Python 3.11 or newer from https://www.python.org/downloads/ and create the virtual environment with it, naming the version explicitly.

python-streamlit.confirm: After activating .venv, python --version prints Python 3.11 or newer.

python-streamlit.title: Creating .venv fails with an ensurepip error
python-streamlit.symptom: python -m venv .venv stops with “Error: Command '['…/.venv/bin/python3.11', '-m', 'ensurepip', '--upgrade', '--default-pip']' returned non-zero exit status 1.”
causes: The Python installation's built-in pip installer (ensurepip) fails inside new virtual environments. This is a problem with that Python installation, not with the project.

diagnose.text: Find out which Python installation the command used.

fix.text: Create the environment with another Python 3.11+ installation, for example from the python.org installer, which on macOS adds /usr/local/bin/python3.11. --clear replaces the half-created .venv folder.

python-streamlit.confirm: The command finishes silently, and after activating .venv, pip install -r requirements.txt starts downloading.

observed.environment: macOS 26.2 (arm64) with Homebrew Python 3.11.15; the python.org Python 3.11.7 on the same computer worked
observed.during: pnpm verify:generated, while creating the virtual environment

python-streamlit.title: “Activate.ps1 cannot be loaded because running scripts is disabled”
python-streamlit.symptom: On Windows PowerShell, .venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1 fails with a message about running scripts being disabled.
causes: PowerShell's execution policy blocks .ps1 scripts, including the activation script.

diagnose.text: The message names Activate.ps1, which confirms the virtual environment exists and only activation is blocked.

fix.text: Skip activation and run the environment's own Python directly. It uses the packages in .venv exactly as activation would.
The project's setup steps also mention Set-ExecutionPolicy. That changes a PowerShell setting for your user account; the commands above work without changing any setting.

python-streamlit.confirm: The app starts and the browser opens it.

python-streamlit.title: pip says “externally-managed-environment”
causes: pip ran with the system's Python instead of the project's virtual environment.

diagnose.text: Check where Python is running from. Inside the virtual environment the path ends with .venv.

fix.text: Activate the virtual environment first, or call its Python directly.

python-streamlit.confirm: pip install -r requirements.txt runs and installs into .venv.

python-streamlit.title: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'streamlit' (or 'pandas')
python-streamlit.symptom: Starting the app or the tests fails with ModuleNotFoundError naming streamlit, pandas, altair or pytest.
causes: The virtual environment is not active in this terminal, for example because it is a new terminal window.
Installing the requirements failed or was skipped.

diagnose.text: Check whether the package is installed for the Python you are using.

fix.text: Activate .venv again in this terminal, then install the requirements. For the tests, also install requirements-dev.txt.

python-streamlit.confirm: python -m pip show streamlit prints the installed version, and the app starts.

python-streamlit.title: “streamlit” is not recognized
python-streamlit.symptom: streamlit run app.py fails with 'streamlit' is not recognized (Windows) or command not found: streamlit.
causes: The virtual environment is not active, so the terminal can't find the streamlit command installed inside it.

diagnose.text: Check that you are in the project folder and that .venv exists there.

fix.text: Activate .venv, or start Streamlit through Python, which finds it inside the environment.

python-streamlit.confirm: Streamlit prints the local address and the browser opens the app.

python-streamlit.title: The app opens on port 8502 (or Streamlit says the port is not available)
python-streamlit.symptom: Streamlit prints http://localhost:8502 or a higher port instead of 8501, or stops with “Port 8501 is not available” when you chose the port yourself.
causes: Another Streamlit app is already using port 8501. When you don't choose a port, Streamlit 1.66 moves to the next free one; when you set one with --server.port, it stops instead.

diagnose.text: Look for other terminals that are still running streamlit run.

fix.text: Use the address Streamlit prints, or stop the other app with Ctrl+C in its terminal. If you set a port yourself, choose a free one.

python-streamlit.confirm: The app opens at the address Streamlit printed.

python-streamlit.title: pip install fails with connection errors or times out
python-streamlit.symptom: pip prints “Could not fetch URL”, “Max retries exceeded” or a timeout while downloading packages.
causes: There is no internet connection, or it dropped during the download (the packages are several hundred MB).
The network only allows access through a proxy.

diagnose.text: Open https://pypi.org in a browser on the same computer to check that the package index is reachable.

fix.text: Reconnect and run the same command again; packages that finished downloading are reused. On a network that needs a proxy, ask the network administrator how to configure it.

python-streamlit.title: python -m pytest shows failures after I changed something
python-streamlit.symptom: pytest prints F for failed tests and an assert line comparing two values.
causes: You changed a calculation, a message or a rule that a test checks.

diagnose.text: Stop at the first failure to read it calmly: the test name, the file and line, and the two values that differ.

fix.text: If the change was a mistake, fix the code. If the new behaviour is what you want, update the expected value in the test and explain the change in your report.

python-streamlit.confirm: python -m pytest reports that every test passed.
